output.brief: Store 14's rising shrink is not yet shown to be a real rise in losses. The figures for the first three quarters are estimates extrapolated from partial cycle counts, and they carry roughly ±0.6 points of error per quarter. Chain-wide, about half of the stores showing two consecutive rises of this size (13 of 27) were not confirmed by the year-end full count. Store 14's own full-count shrink has been 1.5–1.8% for three years. Recorded shoplifting incidents rose at every store after the incident app launched on 1 April, so the store's 6, 11 and 15 do not prove more theft. The ethics-line tip was checked against CCTV and was not substantiated. Sales mix has not changed. The self-checkout and bus interchange explanations fit the timing but are not separated from the estimate error. Neighbouring stores 9 and 22 are flat or falling, which mildly supports a store-specific change, but they don't settle it. Next steps: keep store 14 in the 7 December full count and reject the proposal to drop it. Hold off on a guard, on pulling the lanes, and on any action against the night stocker until the count result is in. Then compare the count with the interim figures and target the real cause. I'm fairly confident in this, though the cause itself is unresolved.
